’I don’t even know how to feel right now,’ Kent said inwardly, a part of him feeling very impatient.
He had just read that the hierarchy he created before leaving the Star Realm had shattered.
Initially, he believed the Evil King’s influence still remained in all Three Heavens.
However, it became clear to him when he discovered that only the Skull Race, now an evil race, still had him in their hearts.
The rest in all seven gateways had abandoned him.
Even in the first heavens, only one race still held him in their heart.
This meant the second and third heavens had long since abandoned him and his rule.
A part of him wanted to let them be.
However, after he rationalized and started thinking straight, he knew that leaving them to do as they pleased would be bad for the outside universe.
The star beasts aren’t dead.
Even now, the Infinity Universe is being invaded from time to time as the seals that bind them in the star gateway weaken.
If that is allowed to continue, in a few years’ time, the Infinity Universe would be invaded again, and the entire universe would plunge into chaos.
He doesn’t want that to happen, not when the Dark Queen, perhaps now an Empress, and her fiends, among other horrors, remain at large.
So his soul warriors are making sure all-star beasts in the Lower Heaven are dealt with and converted into beings he would have absolute control over.
The only problem was that once they conquered the Lower Heaven, moving to the High Heaven and the Supreme Heaven would be difficult.
He doesn’t have the power to face gods, Supremes, and Celestials at the moment.
There is a chance he may even encounter Pseudo-Primordials.
He and his subordinates cannot handle those kinds of odds.
However, everything changes if he were to awaken a Grand Shaman and put him or her in charge of conquering the Star Realm and other banished realms like the Tormented Chaos Abyss.
’The possibilities are endless.’
Kent made a fist and smiled.
He looked at the quest again.
’24 forbidden beasts, huh.
I already have Kharvok, meaning there are 23 more to go.
As for the others, I would surely be happy to commit a massacre.
After all, I need blood Essence.’ Kent formed some plans in his head, and a roadmap was drawn.
’Tower, purchase Bloodline Tempering Pills and Foundation Strengthening Pills for four people.’ Kent planned on making his four Grim-contracted beasts strong enough to carry out a mission for him.
Plans had changed, and so he must adapt.
[This might be the best time to tell the master that he owes me billions in Tower Points.]
’What?
When did I use my 97 billion Tower Points?’ Kent’s eyes widened.
Before leaving for the mission, he checked his Tower Points, and he had close to a hundred billion.
So far, he had used less than a million.
So where did the rest go?
[Goddess Vexthra and the other legion members made some purchases that involved borrowing from me.
Since what they required was important, I allowed them to owe me.
Now, I believe the master owes me 112 billion Tower Points.
However, since the master needs these pills, I will add them to his tab, and when the master is out of here, we will make arrangements on how to pay me back.]
Kent could only remain seated there, his expression a bit dark.
He wasn’t angry, just worried that something major might have happened, and his wives had no choice but to spend that much on a treasure.
’I need to hurry,’
Taking a deep breath, he told Tower to purchase the pills.
Afterward, he handed them over to the four demigods with whom he had signed the Grim Contract.
"Eat these pills.
When you’re done, I have missions for you."
They nodded and started to cultivate the pills.
Since it had come down to this, Kent knew he had to assign one of the quests to these Grim-contracted beasts.
Since he must handle both the forbidden and abominations, he knew he had to assign the rest of the demigods to his other contracted beasts.
At the end of the day, it was either they submit or they die.
Kent didn’t want them to die, but he also trusted and believed that even if they died, they would still be his.
His Necromancy class had been dormant for a while now.
It wasn’t because he couldn’t create more undead; it was just that he had no reason to do so.
The Planet Killer Dungeon wasn’t difficult enough to pose a threat to his legion, so he lets them be.
Now, however, Kent sensed something bad was about to happen, and so he was being pushed to amass an army.
Before coming to the Star Realm, he believed he was here to fight his way to Elina.
While that was true, he now realized there was a much bigger threat he had to handle first.
’I don’t know what is coming, but I pray that when it arrives, I will have the strength and army to handle it.’
Kent turned toward Kharvok and saw he was already halfway through his innate body awakening.
Once he is done, his strength would double.
Kent planned to go with him to hunt down the other forbidden and make them his contracted beasts.
Once that is handled, he will proceed to the Central Region and deal with the demon there.
Becoming a Sword Divine requires him to attain Absolute Heavenly Sword Energy and kill the Crimson Blood Demon General.
Attaining the Absolute Heavenly Sword Energy is possible and quite easy, really.
He had witnessed someone use it before during his life as the Ruthless Bandit.
So he would be learning it before meeting that demon.
Once he defeats it and becomes a Sword Divine, the four abominations would be next.
Since they are a terror, per what Yggzrael said, then he must prepare well to meet them.
Kent moved away from his beast, currently cultivating, and retrieved a small black pagoda.
It was very small; however, Kent knew it had to be awakened first before it would function.
’Tower...’
[The master is required to add a drop of his blood essence to awaken the Undead Pagoda.]

chapters.title: Chapter 1610: Undead Pagoda
paragraphs: The Astryx were the most peaceful race in all of the forgotten Universe.
In their millions of years of living, no Astryx had ever killed, not even animals such as goats or fowls. They believed in the notion that all life matters, and so all life must co-exist.

Then the Corrupted King came, and everything they knew and loved was thrust into corruption. As beings who lived within the stars, they saw everything that happened, and inasmuch as they wished for life to be spared, they could only watch.
Eventually, every life was corrupted, and so the Corrupted King turned his sight on them.
As beings who had never killed, they had nowhere to run and no warriors to save them. They were basically helpless before the terror of the Corrupted King.
The moment he reached their doorsteps, all life would be lost.
They knew that, and so they made peace with themselves. However, nine of them resisted. They were okay with being killed, but being corrupted wasn’t something they wanted.
So on that day, nine deaths, the first ever to happen among the Astryx, occurred, and it was nine people killing themselves.
Legend has it that when the Corrupted King arrived, all Astryx were corrupted and joined the Corrupted Legion, a legion said to have the power to bring down an entire universe.
However, legends also speak of the awakening, the day nine untamed warriors, ones forged in the dark flames of death, became weapons that cannot die.
That day, the first undead were born, wielding power over both life and death.
Legends speak of the day nine undead warriors stood facing a legion of hundreds of billions.
The forgotten books highlighted the smiles on their faces when they dove into battle, and for 6000 nights, a great battle rocked the forgotten universe, breaking its foundation for good.
The Corrupted King fell, and so did his Corrupted Legion. All that stood after this carnage were nine undead warriors, beings forged for one thing and only one thing: Battle.

Kent stood before nine stone statues, each oozing an aura that made his skull tremble. When he dropped his blood on the Undead Pagoda, his entire body vanished, and he appeared in this strange place where a book lay on a table.

On the pages, he read a narrative that describes the birth and legend of the First Undead. According to the book, in the vast multiverse, the first-ever undead were beings who chose to end their lives rather than be corrupted.
They had never killed even a bug before, yet they killed themselves rather than be corrupted. In the books, he saw when they were reborn and what they accomplished afterward.
Right after he finished reading the book, he was taken to a place where nine statues stood before him.
"I believe these are the nine undead I saw," Kent muttered, looking from left to right. Each undead he saw was unique in its way.
Each looked terrifying, more terrifying than anything Kent had ever seen. However, the statues standing before him, while intimidating, looked more human to him.
It made him wonder whether these were the human forms of the nine terrifying beings he had read about in the book.
He turned around to look for something else. Unfortunately, it was completely dark. The statues were the only visible things there.
Kent sighed, looking at the suffocating darkness before him. "Makes me wonder why I am seeing all—ouch,"
Suddenly, a pebble struck Kent from behind, causing him to turn and look at the perpetrator. Turning back to the statues, he saw a man seated on the shoulder of the first statue.
Soon, his gaze snapped to the other statues, and there, seated in different postures, were the Nine Undead, the same beings who faced an army of an entire universe and walked away unscathed.
Kent’s heart skipped a beat when his gaze landed on these people.
He sensed no pressure coming from them, yet he felt like he was merely a bug standing before overlords.
It must be noted that Kent has the willpower of a demigod chaos dragon, a celestial swordsman, and a celestial evil king. But despite all that, he looked like a bug before them.
But who is Kent, if not one of the most dangerous beings in the universe? His dragon intent moved, and the inferiority he felt was lessened by a few percentages.
There are five males and four females.
"Are these seniors the First Undead?" Kent asked, his voice steady.
A beauty with long, silky white hair and sorrowful eyes giggled and waved her hand, causing Kent to float up. He did not panic, but he didn’t feel safe either.
He was ready to unleash a terrible soul attack at a moment’s notice, even if that was the last thing he would do alive. Thankfully, he did not have to do so, since the lady meant him no harm.

"We are indeed those Nine Undead. However, this isn’t our true body nor soul. In fact, what you are looking at right now are our 100th shadows. If we appeared in our 99th shadow, you would be broken and half-dead on the floor by now."
Kent’s brow furrowed.
Seeing this, the nine undead laughed.
Bisa, a long, green-haired, handsome man that Kent would later get to know as the Plague Tyrant, spoke:

"I can tell you are someone with great potential, kid, perhaps the best in the entire universe. However, you have to know that in the vast multiverse out there, there are those who have powers far beyond your understanding.
What Edha said was a bit exaggerated. The current version of us you are looking at right now is akin to a demigod in your universe, and that is just our 100th shadow."
’Just demigods, and I feel so small. How the hell are they this powerful?’
The man seated on the first statue seemed to hear what Kent was thinking.
"Don’t beat yourself up, kid. The current you has yet to meet your true potential as a true immortal. In fact, you haven’t even reached 20% of your potential yet, so it is normal to feel small."

He cleared his throat and nodded with a smile on his face. "You are an Absolute, so you have no limit to yourself. The only thing holding you back is your own self. You must challenge yourself and unlock more of your hidden potential."
Kent was taken aback.
To him, he believed that after he became an Absolute, that was all. But now, he never expected to hear this.
’When Paragon said I have yet to meet my true potential, he wasn’t kidding.’ Kent smiled. ’Hold on a minute, how did Paragon know I had yet to meet my potential?’
Suddenly, an image of a white-haired young man appeared in his mind, prompting him to wonder just what kind of existence the Paragon is.
’If I am merely at 20% of my potential, then how can I become 100% even though I am an Absolute?’
Realization finally dawned on Kent. ’This universe is not large enough to require me to go to the extreme. The void beast I faced before isn’t strong enough for me to go to the extreme.
This can only mean one thing: I am not preparing to fight the Void Beasts or the Forsaken Race. My enemy isn’t going to be like the previous ones I’ve faced.’
He lifted his head and looked at the nine people staring back at him with varied expressions.
"My name is Kent Madson, the Primordial Chaos Dragon, the Genesis Swordsman, the Divine Beast Tamer, and the King of Evil. I pay my respects to the Nine Undead Generals."
They all smiled, and Kent felt something within him snap.

chapters.title: Chapter 1611: Ancient Beings
paragraphs: Kent understood one thing.
He knew that the current him wasn’t strong enough to awaken these people and command them to fight for him. He may have become their master, but he cannot use them just yet.
Even before he could face them, they had to send the shadow of their shadow of another shadow all the way to the 100th shadow simply to not overwhelm him with their power.
That kind of power isn’t one he can unleash just yet.
But that is fine.
He already has more than enough legions under his command. These beings wouldn’t even have anything to do to aid him, even if he could release them now.
However, there is one thing he can do: utilise their knowledge for personal growth.

He recognised that all nine of them are ancient beings from a different Universe known as the forgotten Universe. Aside from that, from the way they spoke, it seems they had been conscious for a while now, meaning they know quite a lot.
So why not let them guide him in matters he doesn’t know? This way, he can grow much faster and release them. While fighting for him would be nice, Kent also wants his legion to live good lives.
Away from fighting for him, he wants them to be able to build a life for themselves.
So as he faced them, the need to know more burned in his heart.
The dark-haired man on the first statue smiled upon hearing Kent introduce himself. "So you are him, huh?" his eyes sparkled.

"We have witnessed your life in full, Chaos Dragon, and I have to say, of all the talents we have seen in our limitless lives, you are within the top 13, perhaps ranked even at the top." The man suddenly paused, and his eyes narrowed.
"Did you just say you are the Genesis Swordsman, the Divine Beast Tamer, and the King of Evil?"
Kent smiled and nodded. "They were my incarnations."
"Wow. That is unexpected," the nine undead generals turned and looked at each other.
The man on the third statue, a rather calm man from the look in his eyes, asked:
"If you are the Genesis Swordsman, the Divine Beast Tamer, and the King of Evil, then you would happen to also be the smartest man to ever walk the face of this universe, Pill Celestial Kevin Sage."
Kent smiled and nodded.
"What about the Nine Underworld Flames Blacksmith?"
"Yet to remember that life... at least if it were me. But what I do know is, including the life of the Primordial Chaos Dragon, I have lived 13 lives in total."

Kent could see the shock and excitement appear in the eyes of the Nine Undead Generals. Clearly, they had witnessed all his lives, and perhaps that was why he ranked among the top 13 greatest of all time.

Kent had already seen his life as Lord Genesis and the Ruthless Bandit in full, and so he knew he was indeed the greatest in that era. So he wouldn’t be that shocked if he was all 13 they had witnessed.

"This is interesting. To think our first ever master would be the person that made us stop and stay in this universe," the lady seated on the 6th statue said, recalling when the undead pagoda they were in drifted soundlessly for years until they arrived in this universe.
"Tell me, Kent Madson, what do you want to know? You must remember that we are beings of great power. However, even with that power, we cannot violate the rules of this universe.

Of course, as you grow stronger, those rules can be bent somehow to reveal some secrets that you would find very interesting. So ask; if we find your questions within reason, we will answer them all."

Kent nodded and asked the first question that came to mind, "What cultivation base are you seniors currently at? I can tell that you are way past the Celestial stage and perhaps even above the Pseudo-Primordial stage. So are you at the Primordial Stage, and if yes, how did you get there?"
If it were before Kent recovered his memories to the peak in two lives, he wouldn’t have asked this question. However, things are different now; he knows way more than ordinary folk.

The seventh lady smirked. "Your question can be answered partially. First of all, know that the Celestial stage is not the peak, and neither is the Pseudo-Primordial. In fact, I don’t even think the 4th Tier is the peak."
Kent said nothing and waited for more context, but none came. He then realised that was all the lady had planned to say.
’4th Tier, huh?’

He saw somewhere before that the 1st Tier is the Mortal Stage. That starts from Root Awakening all the way to Heavenly Ascension. The 2nd Tier starts from Empyrean to Immortal Lord. The 3rd Tier starts from a demigod all the way to a Celestial.
’So the 4th Tier is probably the Primordial Stage, and perhaps there are higher tiers after that. But if that is the case, then does that mean there are Primordials in this universe?’
"Don’t stress yourself, Kent Madson. In due time, everything will be revealed. Now, ask questions that will benefit you, and hurry—your time here is slipping."
"Okay." Kent thought for a moment and asked a question that would indeed benefit him.
"You mentioned I have not yet reached 20% of my potential. Since that is the case, can you tell me how I can push that a little bit higher?"
"A good question," the man on the 5th statue nodded.
"First of all, I would advise you to temper your body. I can tell you have attained the Nirvana Body. That is okay for someone your age and cultivation.

However, if you want to move ahead, then walk the Nine Nirvana Tempering Path and temper your body in the essence of true Nirvana Flames. We have located all nine Nirvana Flames and will give you the locations when you ascend to the Immortal Realm.
Second, cultivate your Beast Taming abilities and unlock an innate skill called Symbiosis. This skill allows you to inherit a percentage of the contracted beast’s power.
Unlike how you can inherit their soul strength, Symbiosis will instead allow you to inherit their strength and abilities, enabling you to wield immense power without having to do much.

Of course, it also depends on how strong your body and meridians are. This means you must exceed the Nirvana Body and step into the Immortal, God, Supreme, and Celestial Body. We have a technique that can aid you, but you are not strong enough for it just yet.
Find one and use it to reach the God Body, and then we will give you that technique.

Third, it would be advisable to pay attention to your many lives. There is more to gain there, especially the experience you have acquired in all those lives. Utilise them well and never stop chasing after more strength.
I don’t know why you were made our master, but I do know that if we are here, then danger is coming. So challenge yourself, and whenever you see an opportunity, grab it.
Lastly, pay attention to your legion’s growth. I have a feeling that when you ascend, something good will happen to you."
Kent nodded, taking everything the undead general said to heart.
"Another question," Kent said, turning toward the first undead general. "Aside from True Sword Energy and Absolute Sword Energy, are there others?"
The question was directed to him simply because he was the only sword wielder among the nine undead generals.
He smiled and nodded. "Indeed. There are others."

"Okay." Kent thought for a moment and asked a question that would indeed benefit him.
"You mentioned I have not yet reached 20% of my potential.
Since that is the case, can you tell me how I can push that a little bit higher?"
"A good question," the man on the 5th statue nodded.
"First of all, I would advise you to temper your body.
I can tell you have attained the Nirvana Body.
That is okay for someone your age and cultivation.
However, if you want to move ahead, then walk the Nine Nirvana Tempering Path and temper your body in the essence of true Nirvana Flames.
We have located all nine Nirvana Flames and will give you the locations when you ascend to the Immortal Realm.
Second, cultivate your Beast Taming abilities and unlock an innate skill called Symbiosis.
This skill allows you to inherit a percentage of the contracted beast’s power.
Unlike how you can inherit their soul strength, Symbiosis will instead allow you to inherit their strength and abilities, enabling you to wield immense power without having to do much.
Of course, it also depends on how strong your body and meridians are.
This means you must exceed the Nirvana Body and step into the Immortal, God, Supreme, and Celestial Body.
We have a technique that can aid you, but you are not strong enough for it just yet.
Find one and use it to reach the God Body, and then we will give you that technique.
Third, it would be advisable to pay attention to your many lives.
There is more to gain there, especially the experience you have acquired in all those lives.
Utilise them well and never stop chasing after more strength.
I don’t know why you were made our master, but I do know that if we are here, then danger is coming.
So challenge yourself, and whenever you see an opportunity, grab it.
Lastly, pay attention to your legion’s growth.
I have a feeling that when you ascend, something good will happen to you."
Kent nodded, taking everything the undead general said to heart.
"Another question," Kent said, turning toward the first undead general.
"Aside from True Sword Energy and Absolute Sword Energy, are there others?"
The question was directed to him simply because he was the only sword wielder among the nine undead generals.
He smiled and nodded.
"Indeed.
There are others."

chapters.title: Chapter 1612: Soul Battle (1)
paragraphs: "I can tell you are currently at the True Sword Energy stage. While that is admirable for someone your age, learning you were Lord Genesis now makes me wonder why you aren’t yet at the Absolute Sword Energy stage."
Kent scratched his head, a smile appearing at the corner of his lips.
"Forget it. I will teach you Absolute Sword Energy, then you can be on your way. That said, aside from Absolute Sword Energy, there are Extreme, Ultimate, and finally Primal."
Kent nodded, the smile on his face displaying how happy he was. This encounter had already benefited him in ways he could not bring himself to understand.
Initially, he planned to paint a warlord he met during his time in the Star Realm back when he was the Ruthless Bandit. That warlord had Absolute Sword Energy.
They fought, and he was defeated.
However, he didn’t lose either. He managed to understand the sword energy the warlord used, and that was what he planned to use to learn Absolute Sword Energy.
He would paint him, manifest him, and cross swords with him again. This would have pushed him to understand it better.
Now, he had no reason to spirit paint that person, whom he believed might still be alive and somewhere in this realm.
A light flew and merged with Kent’s forehead.

"Your time here is ending, Kent Madson. For now, since you have bonded with the Undead Pagoda, you can come here whenever you have enough time. I believe a year on the outside would give you a minute in here.
Accumulate an hour before you return here. I believe by then you will be several times stronger to meet our 99th shadows."
Kent nodded. "Thank you, seniors. I will grow stronger so I can free you from this place. That said, if you need anything, I will be available to provide it for you."
They nodded, and he was gone.

"Teye, looks like you have finally met your match. This kid is a bundle of talent when it comes to swordsmanship," the man seated on the second statue addressed the first man who gave Kent the method to cultivate Absolute Sword Energy.
Teye, the one Kent would come to know as the Death Sovereign, smirked and said:

"You would do well to address him the right way. He is now our master, and as beings with no purpose, perhaps he will have a good use for us. As for his talent, I saw it firsthand when he managed to glimpse into the 4th tier."

"No need to be too serious, Teye. We both know Kent Madson is who we have been waiting for. What I personally never expected was him being the reincarnation of that Archer." The lady seated on the 9th statue blushed.
"By the dead gods, this is like a dream come true."

The eight undead generals turned and looked at her, but said nothing. They knew who she was talking about, and they remembered vividly how obsessed she was with that archer whose arrow could travel to both the past and the future.
He was one of the rarest warriors this universe had ever seen.
To think he was Kent all along.

"Suddenly, I feel like I will be having so much fun again," the lady on the 8th statue said, looking at her slender hands. "Very soon, I will have purpose, and that will be to fight for my new master, the Rejected Prince."
The others nodded.
They had each fancied an incarnation of Kent in the past.

It wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say his many lives were what kept them sane all this time. He had given them someone to admire, like, and love, and so for them, Kent might as well be Lord Genesis, the Faceless Assassin, or even the Chaos Dragon.
Now that they knew he was all of them, they would do their best to guide him toward a future where nobody, absolutely nobody, can contend against him.
"Ocran, why are you so quiet?"
Everyone turned to the handsome man on the 3rd statue. Naturally, he looked like someone who doesn’t talk much. However, given the revelation they had all witnessed, he should at least say something.
After all, he was practically best friends with the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith.
The man named Ocran, the Crypt Warden, turned slowly and looked at his teammates. For a moment, they all expected him to say something. However, he just smirked and vanished from the statue.
"What an uptight guy."
"Leave him be. His personality will return to him when his best friend returns."
The others laughed, and soon they all vanished from the nine statues. They would return when Kent had accumulated enough time to have a good chat with them.
If only they knew it would be sooner than they thought. After all, with the time difference inside the tower, 60 years might as well be months on the outside.
Kent found himself back in Yggzrael’s domain. He exhaled and turned to look at his companions.

Yggzrael and the other three demigods were done using the pills he gave them. Sensing their aura, Kent could tell they had grown at least three times stronger. That was more than enough to make the overlords of the four regions.
He smiled, knowing his strength was steadily rising. He retrieved 12 Grim Contracts and handed them to Yggzrael...

"Go to the other three regions and ensure the demigods there sign the contracts. Those who would resist, you have my permission to kill them. Of course, make sure they understand what they would be missing first.
Once that is done, inform me."
They nodded, and after bowing to Kent, they left for their mission.
Kent turned to Kharvok, who now had an ice cocoon around him. This sight made Kent furrow his brow...

[The master shouldn’t worry. I believe Kharvok has encountered an opportunity and is currently undergoing a mutation. If before he would be coming out two times stronger, then now, there is a chance he would return ten times stronger.]
"Well, I hate weak people, so it is only natural he returns a monster like me," Kent chuckled and decided to let his body relax.
However, the next second, a powerful burst of energy erupted inside his soul sea, causing Kent to widen his eyes. He sat up, and his soul appeared inside the vast, blood-filled soul sea.

There, standing 20 million km from him on a hill, was a beautiful tree about a kilometre tall with interwoven branches and canopy leaves. On its branches, there were varieties of fruits, some coloured orange, green, red, blue, purple, and others.
"This is Lady Kenzie’s Bloodline Skill Tree," Kent recognised the tree at a glance.
While the tree he saw before was much dimmer than this, he knew it was the same tree, and, to his shock, a green-haired lady clad in a translucent green lace dress was seated under it.
There was quite a distance between them, but Kent could tell she was exactly the lady he saw when he absorbed the Green Life Dao Stone.
Suddenly, a wave of refreshing energy came from the tree, making Kent sigh. He even smiled, thinking he was right about the Dao seed.
The next second, however, a humanoid formed from roots and leaves jumped down from the tree and lunged toward him, its speed blinding. More followed suit.
"WHAT—"
Kent lunged forward, his Soul Universe activating despite the shock on his face. He knew it was a battle of survival, and he had to win.
Thousands of spears and swords came from the Soul Universe and appeared inside the soul sea. Kent gestured forward, and they surged at the approaching Plantkins.
[You have awakened a Soul Guardian, the first of her kind. To make her recognise you, add a drop of your blood essence to the gem of her crown.]
[Failure means destruction of your soul.]

chapters.title: Chapter 1613: Soul Battle (2)
paragraphs: Spears and swords flew through the air, stabbing through the approaching Plantkin.

At best, Kent calculated that they were Root Immortals, so killing them wasn’t that stressful. Tower had warned him already, so he knew what had to be done now that the Dao Seed had fully blossomed and wanted to take control of his soul.
Kent had seen the message and knew the first thing he must do was carve a path to the tree standing on the hill, looking majestic, and add his blood to the gem of the crown on Lady Kenzie’s head.
’Is she even Lady Kenzie?’ Kent wondered, his hands moving as swords and spears zipped through the air, killing more plantkin.

’The Lady Kenzie I met looked peaceful and benevolent. She didn’t strike me as the kind of person who would try to take over the soul of another being, especially one who promised to get revenge for her.’
Kent smiled slightly and advanced steadily as more and more Plantkins flew at him.
He tried to use the Soul Map to get close to the tree, but it didn’t work. It felt like there were some laws blocking him from using it.
Now, he had advanced 2 million km, leaving him 18 million more to go.
For now, he saw no need to panic, since the Plantkins coming were rather weak, and they couldn’t hurt him even if he let them.
So Kent moved forward steadily.
Just when he breached the 5 million km distance, the Plantkins coming grew stronger, some rising to the rank of True Immortals.
Kent was stunned for a moment when he saw them grow taller, larger, and far more powerful. Their speed increased, forcing him to adapt as well.
The battle intensified, and Kent knew he had to hurry. However, the closer he got to the tree, the more deadly his foes became.
In fact, when he was halfway there, the first Immortal Lord appeared, causing Kent to wonder what would happen when he was only 100 meters away.

A chill ran down his spine, and for a moment, Kent felt danger. If 10 million km away, he had already started clashing with Immortal Lords, then wouldn’t that mean he would be facing demigods and perhaps gods when he was much closer to the tree?
’I need to hurry.’
He tapped into his Soul Universe, and more weapons surged out.

’Good thing Tower had never stopped creating and improving the weapons there.’ With the kills of his legion now contributing to his horde of Soul Spirits, Kent now had over a million spears at his disposal.
Though temporary, if he could return them to his soul sea before they ran out of soul essence, he could reuse them.
A spear moved through the air, stabbing through three Plantkins, before a root tendril wrapped around it and snapped it in half.
Kent felt a small portion of his soul essence vanish. However, it was an insignificant loss considering the entire Soul Universe was under his command.
More flying spears and swords were shattered, but more kept coming, just like how the Plantkins kept coming.
Kent kept moving, and before long, he was 5 million km away from the tree.
RUMBLE
Suddenly, a rumble rocked the soul sea, and from within the tree, a small leaf flew forward. When it was at a safe distance, it transformed into a wingless tree dragon, oozing the power of a demigod.
Kent’s eyes narrowed, his instincts telling him he must not underestimate this dragon. There was something different about it that made his skin crawl.
However, he didn’t hesitate and sent his swords flying toward it. Kent’s eyes narrowed when, just as the swords closed in, the dragon released a roar, and all 100 swords shattered.
"Oh, that was surprisingly heartbreaking," Kent smirked, knowing his swords and spears couldn’t do much to this dragon.
Thankfully, the spears and swords weren’t the only weapons inside his Soul Universe. Tower had worked overtime to prepare her master for this mission through the Star Gateway.
So when Kent gestured forward, and a cannon mounted on a metallic platform appeared, a smile formed on his face.
With a command, a beam was fired, and the wingless dragon had no idea how to defend against it. A hole was blasted through its head, and it vanished like the other Plantkins.
Kent sighed and put away the cannon, one of the ten that the Tower had created.
She called it the [Soul Erasing Cannon], a weapon that targets the soul directly. Each cannon can fire three beams before it runs out.
With just one beam, the dragon was killed.
However, Kent’s eyes narrowed when, a few seconds after the dragon was killed, it appeared again, this time with an even more powerful aura despite still being a demigod.

"If I didn’t know better, I would say this dragon has reached the mid-level," Kent muttered, his expression tightening as he tried to make sense of what would happen when he killed this dragon three more times.
"If the first one was an Early Demigod and this one is a Mid Demigod, then there is a chance the next would be a High Demigod and then a Peak Demigod.
Would there be a Pseudo-God and then finally God Ascension?" His heartbeat slowed down as the Soul Erasing Cannon appeared again and charged an attack.

"This is my soul sea, so using the meteors and asteroids would be a bad idea, unless I want to kill myself in the process. This means I cannot use them, and I most certainly cannot use the Finger of Destruction, Claw Art, or even the Divine Flame Armament."
Kent gestured forward, and the beam fired, killing the dragon again.
"But if my strongest attacks can’t be used, or else I risk hurting myself, then does that mean I would have to depend only on my Soul Universe? What about the Universe Breaking Fist?"
2 million km remained, and Kent could see the dragon come again. A second later, the leaf transformed into a dragon, and as he anticipated, a High Demigod appeared.
He killed it and continued to advance.
Soon, a Peak Demigod appeared. By then, Kent was 1 million km away.
Two Soul Erasing Cannons appeared and took aim. The beams were fired, and the wingless dragon was blown back instead of being pierced through.
Kent furrowed his brow. "Looks like the Soul Erasing Cannon cannot handle it that easily."
Still, they charged again and fired another beam, this time killing it.
The moment it died, Kent sensed a powerful pressure coming from the tree. He had breached the gap, now 500,000 km away.
"Hold on a minute. Why do I feel like I have overlooked something?"
His eyes narrowed as a Pseudo-God wingless dragon with blue scales and leaf-shaped pink patterns appeared and locked eyes with him.

"When the dragons appeared, I was able to move several kilometres without any hindrance. It felt like with the dragon in the air, I could move forward unhindered. However, the moment they die, a stronger version appears.
In that case, shouldn’t I have contained it when it was at the Early Demigod stage?"
Kent realised he had made a terrible mistake. By keeping the dragon alive, he would have reached the tree much faster. Now, he was up against a Pseudo-God, and he could not use his strongest attacks.
’Ahh, my bad luck...’

chapters.title: Chapter 1614: Soul Battle (3)
paragraphs: The only reason a new tree dragon would appear was if the previous one was killed. If it wasn’t killed, there was no reason for another to appear.
Kent failed to realise this early, and so by the time he did, the dragon he was facing had jumped to the rank of a Pseudo-God.
Trapping this one, rather than killing it, would be extremely hard.
After all, if he were to kill this tree dragon, there is a high chance the next one would be at the God Ascension stage. He most certainly cannot allow that to happen.
So Kent stops and assesses his options.
Since he can’t use any of his trump cards, or else he risks injuring his soul, Kent opts for the next best option, and that is to defeat it in a controlled battle.
So he summoned his dragon wings and took off, his claws already active and gleaming with dragon intent.
ROAR
The tree dragon roared and lunged at Kent with deadly speed. A few seconds later, they collided in a deadly impact that sent shockwaves everywhere.
Kent was pushed back, to his absolute shock.
’That shouldn’t be possible,’ Kent said inwardly as he ducked low, evading a dragon tail attack.

[The master should be aware that this is merely his consciousness manifested as a soul body. Until the master forms a true soul body, he cannot utilise all of his abilities to their fullest potential.]
’I see.’
Kent moved and slashed his claws, aiming for the tree dragon’s neck. However, it moved back and used its long tail to retaliate.
Kent moved back, his annoyed expression showing.
’Ah, I forget how annoying the wingless are with those ridiculously long tails,’ he said inwardly, a smirk tugging at the corner of his lips.
He had always hated the dragons that had no wings.
While they look majestic, their lack of wings makes them seem incomplete. Today, he was reminded of why he hates them and even started a war with them during the primordial era.
Dodging another tail attack, Kent smirked. "Damn it, halfbreed, you had better listen to this monarch and drop down."
[I am afraid the master cannot use the Chaos Monarch’s Sovereignty here.]
"Figured." Kent clicked his tongue and managed to get close to the dragon. With a quick swing, he managed to leave a cut on its body.
However, to his horror, just when the cut appeared on it, a green energy passed over the wound, and it closed. It was as if there hadn’t been a cut just now.
"What kind of healing ability is that?" Kent was mesmerised. Unfortunately for him, he had no time to mess around, since a deadly attack came at him the next second, forcing him to dodge.
He was pushed back, but he managed to recover and pushed the wingless dragon back a few meters.
The fact that the attack he knew could have killed a True Immortal instantly was healed so easily made him wonder just what the hell the dragon was made of.
Suddenly, Kent’s eyes widened.
"Wait a moment. If I am not at full strength here and this dragon can heal this fast, then shouldn’t I use my trumps in a more controlled way?"
For a moment, Kent felt like he had cracked the code and found a loophole. However, he soon found himself stuck behind two questions.
First, how much strength would he need to put the dragon down long enough to break the remaining 300,000 km distance between him and the tree?
Second, if he succeeds in putting it down, how long would the dragon remain down? Its healing ability was surprisingly good, so he must calculate well.
These two questions made him realise that he needed to be able to gauge his strength, and that involves realising his full potential. This way, when he is restricted, he can gauge his strength.
Kent sighed and clenched his fist. "Let’s start small."
He tapped into the [Universe Breaking Fist] and unleashed a blow, making sure he used just 1% of everything. Even the Blood Life and Death Seals he used were at 3 each.
His fist landed on the side of the dragon, sending it crashing down with a powerful thud. "What?"
Kent’s eyes widened when he saw the dragon wince and try to stand, but it couldn’t.
"Don’t tell me that was all it required to put this bastard down," Kent was stunned. He deliberately lowered the power of his attack, yet the results were plain as day.
For a moment, the urge to wait for the dragon to rise back up so he could test his strength again flashed through his mind.
However, he ignored that stupid thought and instead took flight, his speed surging as the dragon roared and winced, probably in pain.
As Kent expected, as he drew closer, no new dragon or plantkin appeared to stop him. This meant that unless the dragon rose again and gave chase, victory was assured.
A few minutes later, Kent landed on the hill. By then, the dragon was back up and had already started chasing him.
However, he only smiled and walked toward the lady seated on the throne under the tree. Looking closely, it appeared that the throne was attached to the tree.
She looked exactly like Lady Kenzie, the same lady he saw inside the Realm of Life.
She sat with her eyes closed and a crown resting on her head.
[The master should put a drop of his blood essence on the gem on the crown.]
Kent nodded and retrieved a drop of his monarch-grade blood essence. He moved forward, and with the wingless dragon 3,000 km out, he smiled and dropped the blood essence.
The effect was immediate.
Kent felt a connection form between him and the entity sitting on the throne.
But that wasn’t all. The moment the connection formed, he felt his body grow stronger and, more importantly, his soul grow safer, despite having soul immunity.
There was no release of overwhelming energy, just a connection that strangely made him feel like even with his head chopped off, he would not die.
"This feeling..." His words vanished when the lady seated on the throne opened her green eyes and finally released a powerful healing energy.
Kent froze in place, his eyes widening as the lady rose to her feet, and while he never expected it, she walked toward him and embraced him.
"Thank you very much, Lord Kent." Kent felt something drop on his chest. He knew it was a tear because, given the height difference, the lady’s face was on his chest.
"Are you Lady Kenzie?"
There was no reply for a minute. When she finally did, Kent paid close attention.

"Yes and no." She said and then elaborated, "I am Lady Kenzie in the sense that I have her memories and, surprisingly, her Dao Seed, which I had no idea how that was possible. However, the me you are seeing now is a new form of life, the first of my kind, belonging only to you."
She paused and smiled, showing how happy she was.
"The current me is what you call a Soul Guardian. My existence is to protect your soul from all forms of threat while also aiding you to the best of my abilities."
Kent furrowed his brow, his mind scanning his memories to see if he had heard of Soul Guardians before. He found nothing.
The only thing that came close was Soul Warriors, which, from what he knew, were also the first of their kind. This made him see the lady in a new light...
"Looks like we have some things to talk about."

chapters.title: Chapter 1615: Soul Guardian Kenzie
paragraphs: Kent turned and saw that the Wingless Tree Dragon was now flying around in his soul sea, almost as if it hadn’t tried to kill him just now.
None of it makes sense, yet somehow everything makes sense.
Lady Kenzie, who was supposed to cease to exist, had surprisingly returned as his Soul Guardian. While having a guardian of the soul sounds cool, what does it mean to be a Soul Guardian?
"First, let’s sit down." Lady Kenzie waved her hand, and a throne appeared for Kent to sit on. He did, and she also sat back down on her throne.
The tree had many colored fruits hanging off its branches.
Kent felt the urge to pluck some and taste them. However, he stopped himself from doing that. Just because it looks like fruit doesn’t mean he should eat it.
"Now, where do we start?"
"You can start by telling me who a Soul Guardian is and what role you are meant to play inside my soul sea." This might just answer all the nagging questions on his mind.
"First of all, you must understand that I am someone who has never existed. My kind has never existed before, simply because the role of a Soul Guardian is linked to a soul body.

Whenever you are attacked using a soul technique, it falls on your soul body to defend your soul from being harmed. Of course, in most cases, those who cultivate their souls as their primary focus develop defence mechanisms to protect them.
All those techniques and methods can be considered guardianship. However, true guardianship involves guarding, protecting, and nourishing the soul.

A Soul Guardian is someone who, on their own, can create measures to protect your soul without you even knowing. If, say, someone were to invade your soul while you are passed out, no amount of soul protection treasures or skills can save you.
However, if there is a Soul Guardian, then I can simply fight the battles that are beyond your reach. I can utilise just about anything inside your soul sea to defend you.
I am linked to your soul, so even if your body is destroyed, as long as there is a guardian as resourceful as I am, you wouldn’t have to worry about dying.
Aside from that, I can cultivate your soul provided you want me to. Naturally, I have the power to make your soul the most protected part of your being."
Kent got the gist of things despite the lady blowing her own horn.

From what she said, if she were to be compared to the Soul Warriors, then her role is to remain inside Kent’s soul while the Soul Warriors roam outside. Their job was to invade other souls, while hers was to protect him.
’But is that all she can do?’ Kent turned and looked at the dragon again.

"I feel like you are not telling me everything. For starters, where did that dragon come from, and more importantly, aren’t you a healer or something? How can a healer defend my soul aside from waiting for me to be hurt so she can heal me?"
Kent smiled.
"Lord Kent is indeed right. I am merely a healer. However, I am also a guardian now, so I naturally have the means to protect Lord Kent’s soul."

"Linda is the first warrior I have under me. She hatched a few days ago and has already reached the rank of God Ascension. If her siblings also hatch, I would have an army large enough to defend your soul."
Kent’s brow furrowed.
"So what is your current rank?"

"I can’t estimate. However, I have reasons to believe my rank would be above the God stage. For now, I have limited features to work with since your soul isn’t strong enough. However, with me here, I will start the soul tempering process. This will push me further to unlocking more abilities."
"Cool. Then what can you do at the moment?"
Lady Kenzie thought for a moment, and then she waved her hand, and they vanished. The next second, they appeared beside Gaap and the Resentful spear Kent purchased at the auction.

"I can sense a very powerful soul hidden within this spear. While the spear itself is broken, I can repurpose it into a dagger or perhaps a rapier and resurrect the weapon spirit’s evolution traits, allowing it to grow again."
Kent widened his eyes, but he knew he had no reason to deprive Gaap of his food. He had been absorbing the resentment from the spear all this while.
Even as he stood there, he could tell Gaap was still absorbing the resentful energy.
Kent was about to reject her proposal when Gaap opened his eyes and said:

"I think you should do that. I have absorbed more than enough resentment to break the second seal. Once that seal is broken, I can further break the remaining seven without its assistance. So transform it into a dagger."
"Are you sure?" Kent asked, and Gaap nodded.
"You already have me as your sword and the new guy as your spear. I believe a dagger is long overdue."
Kent nodded and turned to Lady Kenzie. "Time for you to prove your powers for me to see."
She smiled and nodded.
Kent expected her to form hand seals and perhaps prepare something intricate. However, she merely waved her hand, and a diagram appeared beneath the spear, and soon a cocoon formed around it.
"Done. It would take a couple of days to fully awaken, so you must use the time you have to find a good name. I believe something good would soon come to you."
Kent nodded, but inwardly, he was stunned by how easily she used her abilities. This showed she had long since gotten used to her abilities, so she could use them freely.
"So aside from me, can you aid anybody else?"
"Yes. While protecting your soul is my primary objective, I happen to be a healer, so whoever is connected to you can be healed by me, provided they don’t die outright.
Of course, I also have some fruit that would go a long way toward healing. You don’t need them, since I am the full package. However, your friends would benefit from them."
Hearing that made him happy.
Although Elaine is a good healer, she cannot offer her help unless she isn’t present. However, with Lady Kenzie now inside his soul, unless the person is linked to him, she can assist.
But as she said, she had fruits that would aid others, provided he was there to give them to his friends and legion.
Kent knew there was more he must learn about Lady Kenzie, so he made sure the next hour was spent asking question after question.
After he had learned enough, he went back to Gaap.
"Buddy, I hope you will be available in a few days’ time, say two days from now. We have a huge battle that requires only swordsmanship, so I would need you."
"I will be ready, master. I just have to make sure the first seal has been properly explored before breaking the second. That would take about a day or two."
Kent nodded, and after a few minutes of talking, he returned to Lady Kenzie...
"I am leaving now. If you need anything, feel free to let me know."
Since she can’t leave his soul sea, Kent wanted to make sure she had everything.
He may owe some tower points, but he knew that, aside from being made to go on a terrible quest, he could add more to his debt.
He soon opened his eyes just in time for the first crack to appear in Kharvok’s ice cocoon.

chapters.title: Chapter 1616: Kharvok, The Eternal Frost Devourer
paragraphs: Kent watches as the ice cocoon slowly cracks and comes undone.
Already, he can sense a powerful aura coming out of the cocoon. This made him realise that perhaps Kharvok is coming out as a completely overpowered beast.
From what he had learned from the nine undead generals, he had yet to awaken a skill that would further boost his power through the bond shared between him and his beast legion.
If Kharvok is already this powerful from merely awakening his innate body, then there is no telling just what would become of him when he finally becomes a Monarch.

’I don’t know what kind of experiment that bastard performed on him, but if he is coming out this powerful, then I will claim the others as my forbidden beast companions and make sure he cries blood when I kill the others.

Leaving them would mean I cannot claim the Evil Key to unlock the first Grand Shaman. So all 24 Forbidden Beasts would become mine, and the others would die’ Kent said inwardly, his hatred for Grand Dark Lich Barnabas showing in his eyes.
’At least their bodies would be perfect in upgrading my undead when I return to the outside world.’
With plans set and determination rekindled, Kent waited patiently until the last chunk of ice fell, revealing Kharvok in his human form.
Kharvok emerged as a muscular man with a towering physique, broad shoulders, a massive chest, thick, frost-covered arms, and defined abs.
Kent subconsciously compared this version of Kharvok to his beast form, and for a moment, a smile formed on his face.
’Why are all my subordinates good-looking?’
Not that he planned to have ugly subordinates, but at the rate at which they are all coming out, there is a chance he might just end up with an army of handsome and beautiful warriors.
’Well, their master is as handsome as they come, so it is only natural they all look good.’ In the end, shamelessness won. Kent smiled and focused on the other changes that happened to Kharvok.

He has bright, glowing, icy-blue eyes with slit pupils. He is extremely handsome, with sharp facial features and pale, icy skin, paired with long, wild, silver-white hair that falls to his lower back.
What made him stand out was the single braid messily formed and falling down his back.
’I guess he took after the nature of his element.’ Just as Yggzrael took after his green ice and wood elements, Kharvok had the same look, and what was even more shocking was his attire.

He is clad in a black and dark-blue fur cloak made from ancient beasts. The cloak left his upper body exposed, with heavy ice-forged armoured gauntlets on his arms, and fur waist garments mixed with glacier steel chains.
The urge to lock in battle with Kharvok once again and test his strength overwhelmed Kent’s mind. However, he pulled himself back, knowing they had a mission to handle.
Looking at Kharvok, he could tell he had finally become the kind of Forbidden Beast the Grand Dark Lich had failed to accomplish.
He may have had some success, but compared to the perfect version staring back at him, Kent knew he had won big.
’We are going to have so many adventures once I return from Elina’s Galaxy and ascend to the Immortal Realm.’
"Congratulations, Kharvok, looks like you are finally a true Forbidden Beast."
"Thank you, Young Lord. I will do everything in my power to help you whenever you need me."
Kent smiled and said, "As a matter of fact, we have a mission."
Kharvok nodded and walked forward, every step breaking the ice under his feet. "I am ready to leave now."

"Very well. First, however, what can you tell me about the 23 Forbidden Beasts with domains inside this layer? I know aside from you, there are a hundred others. However, only 23 others have domains."
Kharvok didn’t seem surprised by the question.

After all, aside from him, there are indeed 23 other Forbidden Divine Beasts. They each have a domain they rule, and to be frank, he would rather not face them... at least that was when he hadn’t met Kent.
Now, he is different, and so he has nothing to worry about. Well, there are still a few he would better not offend
"There are indeed 23 others. However, I don’t know if the master and I can take them on. Some are, let’s just say, very terrifying."
Kent smiled, and his wings appeared. "As a matter of fact, I am now more interested. Let’s talk while we fly there."
Kharvok shook his head, a pale smile appearing on his face as he took flight.

Kharvok went ahead to tell him what he knew. "The Young Lord must know that aside from the demon inside the Central Region, there are three other Forbidden Beasts that are even stronger than him, the last I checked.
Also, this list is based on those I know. There may be a few I haven’t met and may even be stronger than this one.

One is the [Reality Bender]. I have never seen this particular Forbidden Beast in action, but from what I learned from the other Forbidden Beasts, it has abilities related to space and time. Honestly, that beast scares me, so I did my best to stay away from it.

The second is the [Chaos Harbinger]. I once witnessed a battle between him and a Monarch Beast. The battle ended within 30 seconds, the Monarch dying and its body being devoured as if it were nothing.
The third is the [Earth Shaker]. For this one, all I can say is that if your strength and defence are poor, you will die before you know it.

Honestly, it would do the master good to fight the beasts inside the Central Region first before facing any of the top ten. I ranked 22nd, by the way. Now, I can count myself in the top 10, maybe top 8"
"Oh, looks like there is a lot of madness hidden here." Kent grinned and asked, "How about the four Abominations?"
"I don’t know much about them, but I learned the Central Region demon had met one before and nearly died. The Young Lord can ask it when you meet."
[Inasmuch as I would love to say Kharvok is exaggerating, I think the master should indeed fight the demon first and become a Sword Divine before facing the Forbidden Beasts and Abominations.]
Tower said, causing Kent to close his eyes and ponder on some things.
’The rewards for killing that demon sure would make me much stronger. However, something keeps telling me it would be one of the deadliest battles I would ever face as a swordsman.’
Kent looked to his left, and after a few minutes of thinking, he changed his mind. "Let’s head to the Central Region first. I must handle that threat before taking on the other missions."

Kharvok nodded, and soon they started flying toward the Central Region. It would take them two days to get there and another day to locate the Crimson Blood Demon General, if he doesn’t locate them first.
[Central Region]

Seated on a red throne bathed in blood, a red-skinned demon with glowing red eyes and dark twisted horns, chains hanging off his body, the Crimson Blood Demon General smirked, looking at two individuals speeding toward his domain.
"So you are the one Lord Dark wanted taken out, huh?" A disdainful look appeared on his face.
"I expected better. Even so, I will end him before the others arrive. Call it the perks of choosing to remain in this layer despite possessing the power to roam in the Chaos Layer."
A great sword beside him trembled, excited that after years, it would finally taste blood.

Already, he can sense a powerful aura coming out of the cocoon.
This made him realise that perhaps Kharvok is coming out as a completely overpowered beast.
From what he had learned from the nine undead generals, he had yet to awaken a skill that would further boost his power through the bond shared between him and his beast legion.
If Kharvok is already this powerful from merely awakening his innate body, then there is no telling just what would become of him when he finally becomes a Monarch.

’I don’t know what kind of experiment that bastard performed on him, but if he is coming out this powerful, then I will claim the others as my forbidden beast companions and make sure he cries blood when I kill the others.
Leaving them would mean I cannot claim the Evil Key to unlock the first Grand Shaman.
So all 24 Forbidden Beasts would become mine, and the others would die’ Kent said inwardly, his hatred for Grand Dark Lich Barnabas showing in his eyes.
’At least their bodies would be perfect in upgrading my undead when I return to the outside world.’
With plans set and determination rekindled, Kent waited patiently until the last chunk of ice fell, revealing Kharvok in his human form.
Kharvok emerged as a muscular man with a towering physique, broad shoulders, a massive chest, thick, frost-covered arms, and defined abs.

’Why are all my subordinates good-looking?’
Not that he planned to have ugly subordinates, but at the rate at which they are all coming out, there is a chance he might just end up with an army of handsome and beautiful warriors.

Now, he is different, and so he has nothing to worry about.

Some are, let’s just say, very terrifying."

Honestly, that beast scares me, so I did my best to stay away from it.

I once witnessed a battle between him and a Monarch Beast.

chapters.title: Chapter 1617: Omniscent Jade Eye
paragraphs: Kent understood two things about the inevitable battle between him and the Crimson Blood Demon General.
The first concerned the nature of the battle as a whole. Kent is a dragon with overwhelming powers. However, to pass and become a sword divine, this battle can only be fought using his sword skills.
That means he cannot use powers like his true dragon form or some spells he had unlocked after recovering Ruthless Bandit’s memories.
This is purely a battle between swordsmen. The only things he can use that would give him a boost are the Chaos Scale Shield, Jade Void Wings and the soul map.
Since those are part of who he is, he can use them.
However, techniques like [Claw Art], [Finger of Destruction], and even [Universe Breaking Fist] cannot be utilised in the upcoming battle.

While he had no idea whether he would be restricted the moment he entered the central region, he knew that if he were to use any of such skills to kill the Crimson Blood Demon General, the quest would fail, and he would fail to become a sword divine.
The second thing was that by killing the Crimson Blood Demon General, he would become one of his legion. He had no idea how that would be managed, but Kent knew killing the demon didn’t mean the end.
He would secure a powerful subordinate, one of the reasons why he chose to face him first before meeting the 23 remaining Forbidden Beasts.
Kent never doubted his instinct, so when they told him not to underestimate the Forbidden Beasts, he knew he had to take that seriously.

Since that was the case, he might as well face what he initially thought would be the most dangerous battle in the tormented Layer. After all, his swordsmanship had stagnated for a while now, so he ought to improve that.

He is now an Immortal, so becoming a sword immortal should be the next move. So he would kill the demon and become a sword divine. Then, after he met the next requirements, he would become a sword legend and, finally, a sword immortal.
’All in due time,’ he thought
Kent decided to buy a flying boat since he had two important things to tackle while en route to the Central Region.

First, he retrieved the [Ten Divine Eye Secret Art] manual and pressed it against his forehead. It was one of the three gifts he received after forming the first Four Grim Contracts with the demigod beast of the Northern Region.
The moment the manual touched his forehead, it dissolved, and a moment later, messages appeared showing he had learned the technique.
Kent wasn’t surprised by how fast he learned the technique since it had been so since the start of his journey.
Turning his attention to the system messages, he started to read.
[You have learned a new secret art: Ten Divine Eyes]
[Ten Divine Eyes]
[Rank: Supreme]
[Description: With eyes that can look past the first layer, gaze into the unknown and discover secrets that elude the ordinary. The stronger your soul, the more you perceive.]
Kent felt his eyes open, and for a moment, he could swear he saw a strange energy come off Kharvok. However, he missed it, prompting him to look again.
However, a different message popped up, taking his attention back to the system interface.
[New mutation discovered: Heavenly Jade Eye + Ten Divine Eye Secret Art]
[Do you want to proceed with this mutation. Yes/No]
Kent didn’t even bother to think things through and just pressed Yes. Already, the Heavenly Jade Eye is overpowered. Having the ability to know something about anything was just too broken.
Now, the Ten Divine Eye Secret Art seems to have also added a layer of power to what he has.
The most important thing was that Kent knew the Ten Divine Eye Secret Art held secrets he hadn’t even discovered yet.
So why not decipher those first before merging them with the Heavenly Jade Eye?
The answer is simply that every mutation makes both skills powerful. So he initiated the mutation, and a few seconds later, his world went blank.
Kent appeared in a space filled with so much darkness that even he started to wonder what kind of danger he had landed himself in.
To his shock, however, a few seconds after he appeared, the darkness started to recede. Soon, he found himself in what appeared to be a library filled with books of different shapes and sizes.
Kent wondered where he had found himself once more. Soon, however, he saw a golden-haired man seated about 50 meters away, so he moved toward him.
Maybe he would give him a good explanation of where he was.
However, just as Kent took a step toward the man, a scene flashed before his eyes, making him shut his eyes, his heartbeat rising.
"What was that?" His heartbeat rose and fell. He opened his eyes and saw the man still where he had seen him. So, shrugging off the sudden flash he felt, he took another step.

This time, the scene moved much more slowly, so he caught the content. In it, he saw himself on his knees, a large red sword stabbed through his chest. Standing before him was a 3-meter-tall red-skinned demon with twisted black horns.
Kent’s heartbeat slowed down.
’That was me, locked in battle with the Crimson Blood Demon General, and from the look of things, he had killed me, or more likely severely injured me.’
Kent felt goosebumps appear on his skin.
Naturally, a bad feeling crept into his mind when he saw the distance left between him and the golden-haired man. He knew taking one more step meant seeing a familiar scene.
The first was already terrifying. How much more agonising would the subsequent ones be?
He knew he had to stop, or else he might see things that would break his mind.
Thankfully, just when he was about to make a decision, the golden-haired man turned slightly and spoke.
"No need for a second step, just one is good enough."
Kent had no time to even get a better look at the man’s face before his eyes opened on the outside, beads of sweat forming on his forehead.
He lifted his head and saw that Kharvok was looking back at him with a concerned expression.
"Relax, Kharvok, I am fine."
Kharvok nodded, and after a few moments, he turned away. Kent sighed and turned to the messages that had appeared.
[Your Heavenly Jade Eye and Ten Divine Eyes have mutated and formed the Omniscient Jade Eye]
[Omniscient Jade Eye]
[Rank: Celestial]
[Description: Eyes that know all and see everything. Nothing can escape your gaze, and no illusion can distort your perception. Also, you can see 2 seconds into the future.
Note: Whatever you see can be changed, provided you have the ability to change it.]
Kent sat there quietly, his expression showing nothing but shock.
He could sense it; his eyes had opened, and now, he could see more than he could before. In fact, now, he could see better than he ever knew possible.
It felt like something had exploded in his head, allowing his perception to go beyond the first and second layers. He could even see into himself, a feat he could not perform before.
Kent turned his head and looked at Kharvok, and for a moment, he was left stunned at what he saw.
[Unique Trait: Heart of Endless Winter]

[Description: Kharvok possesses a second heart formed from condensed chaos frost. This heart continuously absorbs heat from the environment, making the area around it colder with each passing second.]
Kent’s eyes widened further as his gaze penetrated Kharvok’s soul and landed on a bluish, heart-shaped core oozing an extremely cold energy.
Just when he thought that was all, he felt his gaze zoom in on the Ice Heart, and that was when he saw a small, pill-sized, deep blue core hidden within the heart-shaped core.
[You have discovered Ultimate Ice]

chapters.title: Chapter 1618: Crimson Blood Demon General (1)
paragraphs: Unique traits are basically perks one receives based on many factors. Some come from their class, bloodline, innate body, soul strength, and several other factors.

What Kent was staring at came about due to Kharvok’s Ice Elemental affinity. He had already achieved Extreme Ice affinity. However, the shock came in the form of what he sensed hidden inside the [Heart of Endless Winter] trait.
It appeared Kharvok isn’t far from achieving the next stage of elemental affinity: Ultimate Ice.
"Hey Kharvok, say, has something happened to your ice affinity?"
"I don’t know, but let me check." Kent watched as Kharvok formed a ball of ice and started examining it. After a few minutes, he put it away.
"I can sense it has become more potent. Also, I can feel I am much closer to attaining Ultimate Ice."
"I see. Thanks, Kharvok."
Kent never expected these changes to happen, so this was like an eye-opener for him. But he couldn’t help but wonder just what kind of modifications Kharvok went through to attain such powers.
This made him think of Grand Dark Lich Barnabas. ’I will thank him first, then take everything from him before killing him,’ Kent laughed inwardly.
The new [Omniscent Jade Eye] can see 2 seconds into the future.
While many may see 2 seconds as short, in a high-speed battle, 2 seconds might as well be 2 minutes.
A lot can happen in two seconds, and so Kent knew that with how vast his soul sea was, he would abuse this power, especially against powerful opponents.
Seeing how many sword attacks would happen in the next 2 seconds, and creating a counter for them would come in handy for sure.
He spent some more time examining the Omniscient Jade Eye. When he had had enough, he stopped and focused on learning the [Absolute Sword Energy].
With his comprehension speed, learning wasn’t too hard.
It took less than 30 minutes to fully comprehend it. The moment he unlocked [Absolute Sword Energy], his sword intent and Sword Aura had become much stronger, bringing a smile to his face.
He felt a bit safe knowing he was walking into the battle with his swordsmanship at a level he could not move beyond unless he defeated his opponent.
Two and a half days later, Kent and Kharvok arrived in the Central Region. The moment they crossed the border and entered the Central Region, Kent felt some of his power sealed.
He could sense most of his trump cards, such as [Finger of Destruction], [Claw Art], his dragon abilities, and most of the Soul Universe abilities, being restricted.
He retained his sword skills and techniques, along with abilities like Chaos Scale Shield, Soul Map, and others, which he believed did not violate the rules of swordsmanship.
Feeling himself made to wield only his swordsmanship skills made him smile slyly, but he said nothing.
He was already aware of this before coming, so he had prepared.
It would be a battle between a Sword Immortal and a Sword Emperor. While Kent had yet to reach the Sword Divine and Sword Legend stages, he had reasons to believe he wasn’t limited at all.
The only downside was using a sword realm against a sword domain.
He had faced such odds in the past and knew just how frustrating it was. However, if he managed to take advantage of his opponent’s domain, they would be able to have a good battle.
Kent and Kharvok started making their way through the Central Region, heading toward the core.
They met no beasts, a sign that told them this region was only populated by one person, and that was the demon Kent came to kill.
A few hours after arriving in the Central Region, Kent and Kharvok came to a stop, their focus locked on a lone figure standing atop a small hill 2 km away.
"Looks like he found us, Kharvok," Kent said, a calm smile playing on his lips.
For a moment, he took his time to have a good look at the mountain of a demon he was meant to kill using nothing but his sword.
The Crimson Blood Demon General possessed a towering demonic stature, standing over 3 meters tall.
Kent couldn’t determine exactly how tall he stood, but he knew no normal being should be that tall.
Even in his dragon form, Kent only became a few inches taller than in his humanoid form.
This demon was already a few feet taller than a normal demon.

His skin was dark crimson, covered in black, glowing demonic veins that pulsed like molten lava beneath his flesh. Two massive twisted black horns curved backwards from his skull, while chains forged from cursed bloodsteel hung from his shoulders and waist.
His glowing scarlet eyes burned like dying suns, radiating terrifying killing intent as he locked eyes with Kent.
The Chaos Dragon felt like this gaze alone was enough to kill him.
’Killing this demon would be very difficult.’ Kent wasn’t mistaken; he could indeed tell this might be that one opponent every swordsman dreaded ever meeting.

What made him wonder whether this battle was arranged to see if he could grow past Lord Genesis talent as a swordsman was the large, torn wings made of condensed blood energy that spread behind the demon, constantly dripping crimson particles into the air.
It would be both a land and aerial battle, one that would determine many aspects of combat.
’Winning will surely give me the confidence to challenge powerful foes later,’ Kent resolved himself, knowing the time had come.
"Kharvok, buddy, this battle is between me and this demon. I brought you so you can stand guard against any unknown intruders that may try to sneak up on us.
You have my permission to use every means necessary to kill them."
Kharvok nodded. "Good luck, Young Lord."
"I indeed need luck, don’t I?" Kent jested and took flight, his wings unfurling behind him. He had no reason to keep standing there.
The Crimson Blood Demon General saw him move, and he also took flight. A few seconds later, they stood in the air 200 meters apart.
"So you were the one who took what doesn’t belong to you." The Crimson Blood Demon General’s eyes snapped toward Kharvok, who had moved 10 km away, before turning back to Kent.
"Do you know the kind of person you have offended?"
Kent smiled and responded, "I know, and as it stands, I don’t really care. However, I have a question. Are you one of his little experiments?"
Kent used the Omniscient Jade Eye on him, and all he saw was danger and terror. However, that didn’t change the fact that he sensed some form of foreign presence in the Crimson Blood Demon General.
It felt like someone had taken hold of his being and could command him.

"It seems your arrogance will be your downfall, dragon. Though I wonder, how did someone like you manage to tame a beast under my Dark Lord’s control? Even a failed one like him should have been impossible."
"I can tell you and even free you if you just go down on your knees and bow to me."
Kent saw the Crimson Blood Demon General move, and a large red greatsword appeared in his hand, a wide horizontal swing aimed for his neck.
He blinked, and the next second, the Crimson Blood Demon General moved, a large red greatsword appearing in his hand. Just as Kent had foreseen, the attack came for his neck.
Gaap appeared in his grip, and the next moment, a powerful mixture of sword aura exploded out, shredding the trees around them.
